Complete standalone source of the strongly convex theorem

References and publication status for this development

Published source and unpublished extension

Source: Theorem 1, equation (34), and Appendix B of arXiv:2409.07101v2 (27 May 2025), using the ULA estimate of Dalalyan and Karagulyan. The independent parameter- and latent-dimension extension and its proof presented here are unpublished; equal dimensions recover the paper’s displayed bound. The assumption audit explains the joint-potential smoothness condition.

  • Alex Glyn-Davies, Connor Duffin, Ieva Kazlauskaite, Mark Girolami, and Ö. Deniz Akyildiz (2025). Statistical Finite Elements via Interacting Particle Langevin Dynamics. SIAM/ASA Journal on Uncertainty Quantification 13(3), 1200–1227. Audited version: arXiv:2409.07101v2
  • Arnak S. Dalalyan and Avetik G. Karagulyan (2019). User-friendly guarantees for the Langevin Monte Carlo with inaccurate gradient. Stochastic Processes and their Applications 129(12), 5278–5311. arXiv

This generated file concatenates the local definitions and proofs required for the strongly convex particle theorem in dependency order and imports only Mathlib. Its repeated declarations are the same proofs documented in the dependency atlas, which provides the parallel LaTeX derivations for each included source module. The source is intentionally shown in full for independent checking rather than duplicating thousands of exposition paragraphs. Run lake env lean IPLA/Standalone.lean; in a fresh compatible Mathlib project the same source can be checked as Standalone.lean. The final commands print the exact theorem type and its kernel dependencies. This strongly convex standalone bundle does not replace the separate explicit interpolation assumptions of the LSI extension.

The source is a reproducible concatenation of the dependency modules. Every mathematical proof is explained at its original module page in the linked atlas below, with exact source ranges and the same declaration names. Rebuilding the standalone file and compiling it checks that those declarations remain valid as one self-contained proof artifact.
